name: Shemaiah
title: The Lord's Prophet in Judah
summary: Shemaiah was a man of God and a prophet who served in the kingdom of Judah during King Rehoboam's reign. He is best known for warning Rehoboam against going to war with the northern tribes after the division of the kingdom, and for delivering God's judgment when the Egyptian king Shishak attacked Jerusalem. He served as an important prophetic voice during a critical transitional period in Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: Warning Against Civil War
keyEvents.description: After the ten northern tribes broke away under Jeroboam, Rehoboam intended to gather an army of 180,000 men to reconquer them. Shemaiah received a word from God to warn Rehoboam and all Judah not to go to war against their brothers, for what had happened was from the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Parallel Account in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: The same event where Shemaiah prevented civil war between Judah and Israel is recorded in 2 Chronicles, emphasizing the prophet's role as God's spokesperson.

keyEvents.title: Shishak's Invasion and God's Judgment
keyEvents.description: When the Egyptian king Shishak attacked Jerusalem, Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah with a message that the Lord had abandoned them because they had forsaken Him. This led Rehoboam and the leaders to humble themselves.

keyEvents.title: Partial Deliverance After Repentance
keyEvents.description: When Rehoboam and the leaders humbled themselves after Shemaiah's prophecy, the word of the Lord came again to Shemaiah with the message that God would not destroy them completely, but that they would nevertheless become servants of Shishak to learn the difference between serving the Lord and serving foreign kings.

keyEvents.title: Shemaiah's Records
keyEvents.description: Shemaiah was not only a prophet but also a chronicler. His writings, together with those of the seer Iddo, were used as a source for the history of Rehoboam, demonstrating his significance as a historical witness in the kingdom of Judah.

keyEvents.title: Obedience to the Prophet's Word
keyEvents.description: When Shemaiah delivered God's word not to go to war, Rehoboam and all the people obeyed the prophet's message and returned home. This is an important example of a king in Judah listening to and obeying a prophetic word.
